hook: A declassified USAF Mission Report from the 482nd Attack Squadron documenting a 21-hour ISR mission over the Arabian Gulf on August 26–27, 2020, in which an airborne sensor platform observed an unidentified formation of flying objects traveling northeast-to-northwest along the coast before losing track in cloud cover.
why_it_matters: This document is notable as a formally filed military MISREP that treats the UAP event as a discrete reportable line item within a standard operational record — the weather section explicitly names it as a 'UAP EVENT,' indicating the observation was logged using that terminology in official channels at the time. The observation occurred during an active, long-duration ISR mission in the strategically sensitive Strait of Hormuz region, conducted by what appears to be a long-endurance surveillance platform given the 21-hour mission time and SIGINT/FMV collection profile. The inability to regain positive identification after cloud obstruction left the event unresolved, which is the basis for its inclusion in UAP reporting.

key_findings.finding: The aircrew observed an unidentified formation of flying objects traveling northeast-to-northwest along the coast, tracked for approximately two minutes before losing contact in cloud cover.
